---
title: Check freshness
description: Make sure a price is recent enough, without a clock.
---

CKB scripts cannot read the current time, and the oracle never rejects an old price. Your contract
must compare `publish_time_ms` with a time it can prove.

## After your own cell was created

The strongest pattern: the price must be published **after** the block that created the cell being
spent. The script loads that block's header through a header dep, so the time is provable.

```rust
use lean_oracle_common::consumer::published_after;

let header = load_header(0, Source::GroupInput)?;          // header dep of the input
published_after(&feed, header.raw().timestamp().unpack())?; // strictly later
```

The transaction must include the input's block hash in `header_deps`.

## Within a window of a recent block

To require a price no older than, say, 60 seconds, compare it with a recent block the transaction
includes as a header dep:

```rust
let block_ms: u64 = load_header(0, Source::HeaderDep)?.raw().timestamp().unpack();
if feed.publish_time_ms + 60_000 < block_ms { return Err(ERROR_STALE); }
```

This proves the price is at most 60 seconds older than that block. Combine it with a check that the
block itself is recent, for example by using `since` on an input.

## Use your own state

A contract can store the last price time it accepted and require each new one to be later.
Together with the feed cell's forward-only rule, no price can ever be reused.

## Note

A block's timestamp is set by its miner within consensus limits, so allow some seconds of slack.
